newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money eases to 15.0/16.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money eases to 15.0/16.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money eased to 15.0/16.0 percent from 17.0/18.0 percent on Friday morning.
Dealers said the relatively expensive overnight money was driven up by foreign banks' purchase of overnight swaps.
Overnight swaps eased to 4.0/4.5 from a high of 5.0. Tom/next were at 0.70/0.85 points.
"Liquidity isn't really tight. We expect further easing like Thursday in the afternoon," one local bank dealer said.
The central bank supplied 234 billion rupiah on Friday.
One-week money was last taken at 15.5 percent.
Dealers said operators were extremely worry in the early morning as Friday was the last opportunity for people to withdraw money before heading for the long weekend.
The market will be closed for the Moslem Eid al-Fitr holiday on Monday and Tuesday and reopen on February 12.
They said trading was mainly on short-term money only.
By mid-morning Bank Indonesia had not yet announced bilateral SBIs rates.
The average overnight interbank rate on Thursday was 11.23 percent, compared with 10.86 percent on Wednesday.
